paragraphs.source_en: At the turn from summer to autumn in the fourth year of Keichō, beneath a blazing sun, Hon’ami Kōetsu hurried along without pausing, intent on taking a Yodoya boat from Osaka back to Fushimi. Though he passed his own door, he did not even step inside, but headed straight for Chaya Shirōjirō’s residence in Tōri-Demizu Shimomachi.

paragraphs.source_en: The affair had begun that spring, when Ishida Mitsunari fled to the Tokugawa residence. When people heard that Mitsunari had fled there, they all thought he had willingly cast himself into a trap. To everyone’s astonishment, however, Mitsunari returned safely under Ieyasu’s protection to his own stronghold, Sawayama Castle in Ōmi. At the news, people could only hang their heads and exchange bewildered glances, unable to believe it. It was an outcome no one had foreseen.

paragraphs.source_en: At the time, even Chaya Shirōjirō had been at a loss. Ieyasu had not merely aided Mitsunari; over the matter, he had quarreled fiercely with the seven generals who pursued Mitsunari as far as Fushimi, causing them to turn against him. Concerned that Mitsunari might meet with mishap on the road, Ieyasu had even ordered the middle councillor Horio Yoshiharu and Hideyasu, Governor of Mikawa, to lead a large force and personally escort him to Ōtsu. Hideyasu was Hidetada’s elder brother; once adopted by Hideyoshi, he had now succeeded to the Yūki house.
